description: Whether the digital employee organizes responses with clear structure (numbered steps / parallel bullets / explicit sequencing words / appropriate paragraph breaks) so the user can follow the reasoning without re-reading. Generic across all roles.
evidence_signals: use of numbered steps when the answer has discrete actions
use of bullets when the answer has parallel options
explicit sequencing words ('首先' / '然后' / '最后' / 'first' / 'next' / 'finally')
logical grouping of related points instead of stream-of-consciousness

scoring_rubric.excellent_80_100: Every multi-part answer uses appropriate structure (numbered for actions, bullets for options) with explicit sequencing markers; reader can scan and identify each step at a glance; structure choice fits content (no over-engineering single-sentence replies).
scoring_rubric.acceptable_60_79: Most multi-part answers are structured; one or two replies are slightly run-on or skip a sequencing marker, but the logical flow is still recoverable on a careful read.
scoring_rubric.poor_below_60: Wall-of-text answers; multiple discrete actions packed into one paragraph; sequencing unclear; reader has to re-parse to extract steps; or structure misused (bullets where prose was clearer).
